claims.text: Akamai turned its CDN and the Linode cloud it bought in 2022 into a distributed AI inference cloud.
It signed over $2.8B of multi-year cloud contracts in 2026, including $1.8B from a frontier model provider.
It bought the developer cloud Linode for about $900M in March 2022 to add general compute to its edge network.
In October 2025 it launched Akamai Inference Cloud with NVIDIA, starting in 20 locations with NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell servers and BlueField-3 DPUs.
Akamai's Cloud Infrastructure Services revenue grew 39% to $99M in the second quarter of 2026, out of $1.1B in total revenue.
In May 2026 Akamai said a leading US frontier model provider committed $1.8B over seven years to its cloud infrastructure.
By August it had signed multi-year cloud contracts worth more than $2.8B in 2026, including more than $600M over four years from a new US technology customer for robotics development.
Akamai Inference Cloud runs NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPUs with NVIDIA AI Enterprise software and NIM microservices, aimed at low-latency inference close to users.
A Kubernetes-based developer platform ships with vLLM, KServe and NVIDIA Dynamo, and Akamai charges no egress fees.
The service sits on an edge network that Akamai says spans more than 4,350 points of presence.
Akamai said at launch that an expanded rollout beyond the first 20 Inference Cloud locations was underway.
Cloud infrastructure revenue grows much faster than Akamai's total revenue, which it guides to $4.445B to $4.530B for 2026, but still makes up less than 10% of it.
Cloud Infrastructure Services revenue, Q2 2026 = $99M, up 39%
Multi-year cloud contracts signed in 2026 = Over $2.8B
Frontier model provider commitment = $1.8B over seven years
Robotics customer contract = $600M+ over four years
Edge points of presence = 4,350+
Linode purchase price = About $900M (2022)
